questions.question: Define the principal focus of a concave mirror.
answer_steps: Rays of light parallel to the principal axis of a concave mirror, after reflection, all meet at a point on the principal axis.
This point is the principal focus (F) of the concave mirror.

questions.question: The radius of curvature of a spherical mirror is 20 cm. What is its focal length?
answer_steps: $f = \dfrac{R}{2}$

questions.question: Name a mirror that can give an erect and enlarged image of an object.
answer_steps: A concave mirror.
It gives an erect, enlarged (virtual) image when the object is placed between its pole and principal focus.

questions.question: Why do we prefer a convex mirror as a rear-view mirror in vehicles?
answer_steps: A convex mirror always gives an erect, though diminished, image.
It also has a much wider field of view because it curves outwards, so the driver can see a large area behind.

questions.question: Find the focal length of a convex mirror whose radius of curvature is 32 cm.
answer_steps: $f = \dfrac{R}{2}$
$= \dfrac{32}{2} = 16$ cm (positive, since the focus of a convex mirror is behind it)

questions.question: A concave mirror produces three times magnified (enlarged) real image of an object placed at 10 cm in front of it. Where is the image located?
answer_steps: Real image, so $m = -3$; $u = -10$ cm.
$m = -\dfrac{v}{u}$ gives $v = -mu = -(-3)(-10) = -30$ cm. The image is 30 cm in front of the mirror.

questions.question: A ray of light travelling in air enters obliquely into water. Does the light ray bend towards the normal or away from the normal? Why?
answer_steps: Towards the normal.
Water is optically denser than air, so light slows down on entering it and bends towards the normal.

questions.question: Light enters from air to glass having refractive index 1.50. What is the speed of light in the glass? The speed of light in vacuum is 3 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹.
answer_steps: $n = \dfrac{c}{v}$, so $v = \dfrac{c}{n}$

questions.question: Find out, from Table 9.3, the medium having highest optical density. Also find the medium with lowest optical density.
answer_steps: Highest optical density: diamond (refractive index 2.42).
Lowest optical density: air (refractive index 1.0003).

questions.question: You are given kerosene, turpentine and water. In which of these does the light travel fastest? Use the information given in Table 9.3.
answer_steps: Refractive indices: water 1.33, kerosene 1.44, turpentine oil 1.47.
Light travels fastest in water, since it has the lowest refractive index (v = c/n).

questions.question: The refractive index of diamond is 2.42. What is the meaning of this statement?
answer_steps: The ratio of the speed of light in vacuum (air) to the speed of light in diamond is 2.42.
So light travels 2.42 times slower in diamond than in vacuum: about $1.24 \times 10^{8}$ m/s.

questions.question: Define 1 dioptre of power of a lens.
answer_steps: 1 dioptre is the power of a lens whose focal length is 1 metre.

questions.question: A convex lens forms a real and inverted image of a needle at a distance of 50 cm from it. Where is the needle placed in front of the convex lens if the image is equal to the size of the object? Also, find the power of the lens.
answer_steps: A real image of the same size forms when the object is at 2F₁ and the image at 2F₂, so the needle is 50 cm in front of the lens: $u = -50$ cm.

questions.question: Find the power of a concave lens of focal length 2 m.
answer_steps: $f = -2$ m (concave lens)

questions.question: Which one of the following materials cannot be used to make a lens?
questions.explanation: A lens must be transparent; clay is opaque.
option_feedback: Water is transparent; a water drop acts as a lens.
Glass is the usual lens material.
Transparent plastic is used for lenses.
Correct!

questions.question: The image formed by a concave mirror is observed to be virtual, erect and larger than the object. Where should be the position of the object?
options: Between the principal focus and the centre of curvature
Between the pole of the mirror and its principal focus.
questions.explanation: Only an object between P and F gives a virtual, erect, enlarged image.
option_feedback: That gives a real, enlarged, inverted image.
That gives a real image of the same size.
That gives a real, diminished image.
Correct!

questions.question: Where should an object be placed in front of a convex lens to get a real image of the size of the object?
options: At the principal focus of the lens
Between the optical centre of the lens and its principal focus.
questions.explanation: At 2F₁ the image forms at 2F₂, real and of the same size.
option_feedback: The image would be at infinity.
Correct!
The image would be a point at F₂.
That gives a virtual image.

questions.question: A spherical mirror and a thin spherical lens have each a focal length of –15 cm. The mirror and the lens are likely to be
options: the mirror is concave and the lens is convex.
the mirror is convex, but the lens is concave.
questions.explanation: Negative focal length means a concave mirror and a concave lens.
option_feedback: Correct!
A convex mirror and a convex lens both have positive focal length.
A convex lens has positive f.
A convex mirror has positive f.

questions.question: No matter how far you stand from a mirror, your image appears erect. The mirror is likely to be
questions.explanation: Plane and convex mirrors always give erect images; a concave mirror gives an inverted image when you are far away.
option_feedback: A convex mirror also always gives an erect image.
Far from a concave mirror, the image is inverted.
A plane mirror also always gives an erect image.
Correct!

questions.question: Which of the following lenses would you prefer to use while reading small letters found in a dictionary?
options: A convex lens of focal length 50 cm.
A concave lens of focal length 50 cm.
A convex lens of focal length 5 cm.
A concave lens of focal length 5 cm.
questions.explanation: A convex lens of short focal length gives a large virtual, erect image: a magnifying glass.
option_feedback: A longer focal length magnifies less.
A concave lens makes letters smaller.
Correct!
A concave lens makes letters smaller.

questions.question: We wish to obtain an erect image of an object, using a concave mirror of focal length 15 cm. What should be the range of distance of the object from the mirror? What is the nature of the image? Is the image larger or smaller than the object? Draw a ray diagram to show the image formation in this case.
answer_steps: The object must be between the pole and the focus: less than 15 cm from the mirror.
The image is virtual and erect, formed behind the mirror, and larger than the object.

Ray diagram: a ray parallel to the axis reflects through F, and a ray towards the pole reflects symmetrically; the reflected rays diverge, and their backward extensions meet behind the mirror to form the enlarged, erect image.

questions.question:
Name the type of mirror used in the following situations.

(a) Headlights of a car.

(b) Side/rear-view mirror of a vehicle.

(c) Solar furnace.

Support your answer with reason.
answer_steps: (a) Concave mirror: with the bulb at its focus, it sends out a strong parallel beam of light.
(b) Convex mirror: it always gives an erect image and has a wider field of view.
(c) Concave mirror: it concentrates sunlight at its focus, producing a lot of heat.

questions.question: One-half of a convex lens is covered with a black paper. Will this lens produce a complete image of the object? Verify your answer experimentally. Explain your observations.
answer_steps: Yes, the lens still forms a complete image.
Experiment: form the image of a candle flame on a screen with a convex lens, then cover half the lens with black paper; the full image remains on the screen.
Every part of the lens receives rays from every point of the object, so the uncovered half still forms the whole image; it is only less bright.

questions.question: An object 5 cm in length is held 25 cm away from a converging lens of focal length 10 cm. Draw the ray diagram and find the position, size and the nature of the image formed.
answer_steps: $\dfrac{1}{v} = \dfrac{1}{f} + \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{10} - \dfrac{1}{25} = \dfrac{3}{50}$, so $v = \dfrac{50}{3} \approx 16.7$ cm
$h' = m \times h = -\dfrac{2}{3} \times 5 \approx -3.3$ cm
The image is about 16.7 cm on the other side of the lens, real, inverted and diminished (3.3 cm tall). Ray diagram: object beyond 2F₁, image between F₂ and 2F₂.

questions.question: A concave lens of focal length 15 cm forms an image 10 cm from the lens. How far is the object placed from the lens? Draw the ray diagram.
answer_steps: $f = -15$ cm; the image of a concave lens is virtual, on the same side: $v = -10$ cm
$u = -30$ cm: the object is 30 cm in front of the lens. (Ray diagram: the image is virtual, erect and diminished, between F₁ and O.)

questions.question: An object is placed at a distance of 10 cm from a convex mirror of focal length 15 cm. Find the position and nature of the image.
answer_steps: $\dfrac{1}{v} = \dfrac{1}{f} - \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{15} + \dfrac{1}{10} = \dfrac{1}{6}$, so $v = +6$ cm
The image is 6 cm behind the mirror, virtual and erect; $m = -\dfrac{v}{u} = 0.6$, so it is diminished.

questions.question: The magnification produced by a plane mirror is +1. What does this mean?
answer_steps: |m| = 1: the image is of the same size as the object.
The + sign means the image is virtual and erect.

questions.question: An object 5.0 cm in length is placed at a distance of 20 cm in front of a convex mirror of radius of curvature 30 cm. Find the position of the image, its nature and size.
answer_steps: $\dfrac{1}{v} = \dfrac{1}{15} + \dfrac{1}{20} = \dfrac{7}{60}$, so $v = \dfrac{60}{7} \approx 8.6$ cm behind the mirror
$m = -\dfrac{v}{u} = \dfrac{3}{7}$, $h' = \dfrac{3}{7} \times 5 \approx 2.1$ cm: virtual, erect and diminished.

questions.question: An object of size 7.0 cm is placed at 27 cm in front of a concave mirror of focal length 18 cm. At what distance from the mirror should a screen be placed, so that a sharp focussed image can be obtained? Find the size and the nature of the image.
answer_steps: The screen should be placed 54 cm in front of the mirror.
The image is real, inverted and enlarged (14 cm tall).

questions.question: Find the focal length of a lens of power – 2.0 D. What type of lens is this?
answer_steps: Negative focal length: it is a concave (diverging) lens.

questions.question: A doctor has prescribed a corrective lens of power +1.5 D. Find the focal length of the lens. Is the prescribed lens diverging or converging?
answer_steps: $f = \dfrac{1}{P} = \dfrac{1}{1.5} \approx 0.67$ m $\approx 66.7$ cm
Positive focal length: it is a converging (convex) lens.

questions.question:
Arnav was making notes and he wrote down the following statements from his understanding of reflection from curved surfaces.

I. Concave mirrors can produce both real and virtual images depending on the position of the object.

II. Convex mirrors always produce real, inverted images regardless of the object's position.

III. In both concave and convex mirrors, the image location can be determined using the mirror formula $\dfrac{1}{f} = \dfrac{1}{v} + \dfrac{1}{u}$ where f is the focal length, v is the image distance, and u is the object distance.

Choose from the following the correct option that lists the correct statements about reflection from curved surfaces.
questions.explanation: Statement II is wrong: a convex mirror always gives virtual, erect images. I and III are correct.
option_feedback: Statement II is wrong: convex mirrors give virtual images.
Statement II is wrong.
Statement II is wrong.
Correct!

questions.question:
**Assertion (A):** A point object is placed at a distance of 26 cm from a convex mirror of focal length 26 cm. The image will not form at infinity.

**Reason (R):** For above given system the equation $\dfrac{1}{f} = \dfrac{1}{v} + \dfrac{1}{u}$ gives v = ∞.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.
questions.explanation: A is true: with u = −26 cm and f = +26 cm, the mirror formula gives v = +13 cm, a virtual image behind the mirror. R is false: v is not infinite.
option_feedback: Check the Reason again: it is false, because the formula gives v = +13 cm, not infinity.
Check the Reason again: it is false, because the formula gives v = +13 cm, not infinity.
Correct! A is true: a convex mirror forms a virtual image at v = +13 cm. R is false: the formula gives v = +13 cm, not infinity.
Check the Assertion again: it is true, because a convex mirror forms a virtual image at v = +13 cm.

questions.question:
An object is placed 20 cm in front of an optical instrument (shown as a box). A virtual, erect, diminished image forms 10 cm from the instrument, on the same side as the object.

A. Identify the optical instrument.

B. What type of image is formed in this case?

C. Calculate the focal length of the instrument.
answer_steps: A. A concave lens. B. A virtual image.

questions.question:
A Digital Single Lens Reflex (DSLR) camera is used by photographers to take high-resolution photographs. Inside it, a lens forms an image of the object on the camera's sensor.

(i) What type of lens is used in the DSLR camera? (1)

(ii) What type of image is formed on the sensor? (1)

(iii) A photographer is using a lens of focal length f = 50 mm to take a close-up photograph of a small object. The lens projects an image onto the sensor located 60 mm behind the lens. Calculate the object distance. OR A flower is positioned 150 mm away from the camera lens. The actual height of the flower is 80 mm, and the image height on the sensor is 20 mm. Calculate the focal length of the lens. (2)
answer_steps: (i) Convex lens.
(ii) Real and inverted.
(iii) $f = 50$ mm, $v = 60$ mm: $\dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{v} - \dfrac{1}{f} = \dfrac{1}{60} - \dfrac{1}{50} = -\dfrac{1}{300}$, so $u = -300$ mm: the object is 300 mm in front of the lens.

questions.question: A concave lens has focal length of 15 cm. At what distance should the object from the lens be placed so that it forms an image at 10 cm from the lens? Also, find the magnification produced by the lens.
answer_steps: $m = \dfrac{v}{u} = \dfrac{-10}{-30} = +\dfrac{1}{3} \approx 0.33$: virtual, erect and diminished.

questions.question:
(a) Draw a neat labelled ray diagram for the formation of image by a concave mirror, when the object is placed at the centre of curvature.

(b) Write the uses of concave mirror.
answer_steps: (a) A ray parallel to the axis reflects through F; a ray through F reflects parallel to the axis. They meet at C, below the axis.
The image is at C, real, inverted and of the same size as the object.
(b) Torches, searchlights and headlights; shaving mirrors; dentists' mirrors; solar furnaces.

questions.question: No matter how far you stand from a mirror, your image appears erect. The mirror is likely to be
questions.explanation: Plane and convex mirrors always give erect images.
option_feedback: A convex mirror also always gives an erect image.
Far from a concave mirror, the image is inverted.
A plane mirror also always gives an erect image.
Correct!

questions.question: The lens formula is ____.
questions.explanation: For a lens, 1/v − 1/u = 1/f; 1/v + 1/u = 1/f is the mirror formula.
option_feedback: Correct!
That is the mirror formula.
The signs are reversed.

questions.question: Name the type of mirror used in the following situations, with reason: (a) Headlights of a car (b) Rear-view mirror of a vehicle (c) Solar furnace
answer_steps: (a) Concave mirror: it gives a strong parallel beam with the bulb at its focus.
(b) Convex mirror: erect image and a wider field of view.
(c) Concave mirror: it concentrates sunlight at its focus.

questions.question: Draw a ray diagram showing the image formation by a convex lens when an object is placed between F₁ and 2F₁ of the lens.
answer_steps: Ray 1: a ray parallel to the principal axis passes through F₂ after refraction.
Ray 2: a ray through the optical centre O goes straight without deviation.
The rays meet beyond 2F₂: the image is real, inverted and enlarged.

questions.question: The focal length of a concave mirror is 12 cm. Its radius of curvature is:
questions.explanation: R = 2f = 24 cm.
option_feedback: R = 2f = 24 cm.
Correct!
R is double f, not half.
That is f.

questions.question: The image formed by a convex mirror is always:
questions.explanation: A convex mirror never forms a real image.
option_feedback: Correct!
A convex mirror never forms a real image.
The image is always smaller.
A convex mirror never forms a real image.

questions.question: Which mirror is used by dentists to see a large image of the teeth?
questions.explanation: With the tooth between P and F, a concave mirror gives an enlarged, erect image.
option_feedback: A convex mirror makes the image smaller.
A plane mirror does not enlarge.
A concave mirror is used.
Correct!

questions.question: When light goes from glass into air, it:
options: speeds up and bends away from the normal
slows down and bends towards the normal
questions.explanation: Air is optically rarer than glass.
option_feedback: Only a ray along the normal goes straight.
Light passes into the air.
Correct!
That happens from air into glass.

questions.question: The SI unit of refractive index is:
questions.explanation: Refractive index is a ratio of two speeds, so it has no unit.
option_feedback: Refractive index is a ratio.
Correct!
That is the unit of speed.
That is the unit of power.

questions.question: A convex lens forms a virtual, erect and enlarged image when the object is placed:
questions.explanation: That is how a magnifying glass works.
option_feedback: Correct!
That gives a real image of the same size.
That gives a real, diminished image.
That gives an image at infinity.

questions.question: The power of a convex lens of focal length 25 cm is:
option_feedback: A convex lens has positive power.
Convert 25 cm to 0.25 m, then take 1/f.
Use f in metres: 0.25 m.
Correct!

questions.question: Two lenses of power +3 D and −1 D are kept in contact. The power of the combination is:
questions.explanation: Powers add: 3 + (−1) = +2 D.
option_feedback: 3 + (−1) is positive.
Add the powers: 3 − 1.
Correct!
Add with signs: 3 + (−1).

questions.question: According to the New Cartesian sign convention, the object distance u for a real object is always:
questions.explanation: The object is on the left, against the direction of the incident light.
option_feedback: u can be any distance.
Correct!
The object is to the left of the pole.
The object is not at the pole.

questions.question: The refractive index of glass with respect to air is 1.5. The speed of light in glass is:
option_feedback: Correct!
That is the speed in vacuum.
Divide by n, do not multiply.

Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.

R does explain A: an erect image of a wide area is what a driver needs.

Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.

R does explain A: refraction at the surface causes it.

questions.question:
**Assertion (A):** The power of a concave lens is positive.

**Reason (R):** A concave lens diverges light.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.

option_feedback: Check the Assertion again: it is false, because a concave lens has negative power.
Check the Assertion again: it is false, because a concave lens has negative power.
Check the Assertion again: it is false, because a concave lens has negative power.

questions.question:
**Assertion (A):** Kerosene is optically denser than water.

**Reason (R):** Kerosene has a greater mass density than water.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.

Check the Reason again: it is false, because kerosene is lighter than water.

**Assertion (A):** A lens with half of it covered still forms a complete image.

**Reason (R):** Every part of a lens receives light from every point of the object.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.
questions.explanation: The uncovered half still collects rays from all points: R explains A; only the brightness falls.

R does explain A: the uncovered half still collects light from every point.

questions.question: State the two laws of refraction.
answer_steps: The incident ray, the refracted ray and the normal at the point of incidence all lie in the same plane.
For a given pair of media and a given colour of light, sin i / sin r is constant (Snell's law).

questions.question: Write the New Cartesian sign convention for spherical mirrors.
answer_steps: The pole is the origin; the object is placed to the left; distances in the direction of incident light (right) are positive, and against it (left) are negative.
Heights above the principal axis are positive; below it are negative.

questions.question: An object is placed 30 cm in front of a concave mirror of focal length 10 cm. Find the position, nature and magnification of the image.
answer_steps: $m = -\dfrac{v}{u} = -\dfrac{-15}{-30} = -0.5$: real, inverted and diminished, 15 cm in front of the mirror.

questions.question: An object is placed 12 cm from a convex lens of focal length 8 cm. Find the position and magnification of the image.
answer_steps: $\dfrac{1}{v} = \dfrac{1}{f} + \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{8} - \dfrac{1}{12} = \dfrac{1}{24}$, so $v = 24$ cm
$m = \dfrac{v}{u} = \dfrac{24}{-12} = -2$: real, inverted, twice the size, 24 cm on the other side.

questions.question: Describe with ray diagrams the images formed by a concave mirror when the object is (i) beyond C (ii) between C and F (iii) between P and F. Give one use of the concave mirror for each case where possible.
answer_steps: (i) Beyond C: image between F and C, real, inverted and diminished.
(ii) Between C and F: image beyond C, real, inverted and enlarged.
(iii) Between P and F: image behind the mirror, virtual, erect and enlarged.
Rays used: one parallel to the axis (reflects through F) and one through C (reflects back along itself), or one towards P (reflects symmetrically).
Uses: (iii) shaving mirror and dentist's mirror; the focus property gives headlights and solar furnaces.

questions.question: An object 2 cm tall is placed 20 cm from a concave lens of focal length 10 cm. Find the position, size and nature of the image. What is the power of the lens?
answer_steps: $\dfrac{1}{v} = \dfrac{1}{f} + \dfrac{1}{u} = -\dfrac{1}{10} - \dfrac{1}{20} = -\dfrac{3}{20}$, so $v = -\dfrac{20}{3} \approx -6.7$ cm
$m = \dfrac{v}{u} = \dfrac{-20/3}{-20} = \dfrac{1}{3}$, $h' = \dfrac{2}{3} \approx 0.67$ cm
The image is virtual, erect and diminished, about 6.7 cm from the lens on the same side as the object.

questions.question:
In a car showroom, Ishaan noticed that the side mirrors showed a wide view of the road with small, upright images. In the workshop, the headlight had a curved shiny reflector behind the bulb.

(i) What type of mirror is used as a side mirror? (1)

(ii) What type of mirror is used behind the headlight bulb? (1)

(iii) Where is the bulb placed in the headlight, and why? OR Why are images in the side mirror smaller than the actual vehicles? (2)
answer_steps: (i) Convex mirror.
(ii) Concave mirror.
(iii) At the principal focus, so that the reflected rays form a strong parallel beam. OR A convex mirror always forms diminished, virtual images between P and F.

questions.question:
A watchmaker uses a small convex lens of focal length 5 cm to see the tiny parts of a watch. His optician has prescribed reading glasses of power +2 D for him.

(i) What is the power of the watchmaker's lens? (1)

(ii) What is the focal length of his reading glasses? (1)

(iii) Where must the watch part be placed for the lens to act as a magnifier, and what image does it give? OR Why is a lens of short focal length preferred for this work? (2)
answer_steps: (iii) Between the optical centre and the focus (closer than 5 cm): a virtual, erect and enlarged image. OR A shorter focal length gives a larger magnification for small objects held close to the lens.
